title: A New ECP Protocol for the Treatment of cGVHD
official: Extracorporeal Photopheresis for Graft Versus Host Disease: a Randomized Study Comparing One Split Product Versus Two Products' Administration. The EXPRESS Study.
summary: At present, cGvHD is the main cause of transplant-related morbidity in patients receiving allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (allo-HSCT). Extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) has been recognized as a second-line treatment option for steroid-resistant forms or to reduce the immunosuppressant burden. The more commonly adopted protocol consists of performing ECP procedures on two consecutive days every two weeks initially, and then once a month. The investigators hypothesized that a new ECP protocol consisting of one single apheresis procedure on day 1, processing 5000 ml of total blood volume (TBV), followed by product photo-irradiation and split into two equivalent aliquots to be administered on day 1 and 2, respectively, is safe and might improve self-reported QoL of cGVHD patients.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient age ≥18 years
* Diagnosis of incident (\<3 months from diagnosis) or prevalent (\>3 months from diagnosis) cGVHD
* Ability to understand and sign the informed consent form

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient age \<18 years
* Relapse of haematological disease
* Inability to comply with the study
* Patients enrolled in other interventional trials
* Refusal to sign written informed consent to study participation
